summary:
North Dakota stands under the United States national framework for passports, entry and screening; the findings below are those specific to the state.

North Dakota is listed among the worst states for legislation targeting transgender adults in a July 2026 legal-risk assessment published by Erin In The Morning, and among the states that prohibit any change to birth certificates, which forces transgender people to disclose their status when presenting documents.

Birth certificate markers are closed. A 2023 North Dakota law bans all gender-marker changes on birth certificates with a narrow exception for applicants who have had genital surgery. The Movement Advancement Project's identity-document policy tracker describes the surgical requirement as stricter and more explicit than in many other states and classifies North Dakota as a negative-law state. The regulations accompanying the 2023 law were rejected, leaving in place a 2008 regulation that restricts changes to applicants who have undergone a sex conversion operation.

Driver licence and state identification markers are handled separately. The state Department of Transportation updates the gender marker on a driver licence or state identification card on receipt of a letter from a physician or therapist stating that the applicant has completed a permanent gender role transition.

No North Dakota statute explicitly prohibits discrimination on the basis of gender identity, and the state hate-crime law does not cover gender identity.

An April 2023 law signed by the governor and effective 1 July explicitly allows transgender people's use of public bathrooms to be restricted in many state-run facilities.

A law signed in May 2023 and effective 1 July bars schools and government entities from requiring or prohibiting the use of preferred pronouns but requires that transgender students in state-run schools be disclosed to their parents. The 2023 legislative record for HB 1522, an act creating new sections of the North Dakota Century Code relating to preferred pronouns and providing accommodations to a transgender student, records a penalty provision and an emergency clause, with the governor's signature and the last official action filed with the Secretary of State on 9 May 2023. An earlier March 2023 bill requiring parental and administrative approval for preferred pronoun use in state-run schools and classrooms was vetoed. An April 2021 law allows student groups at colleges, universities and high schools to discriminate against LGBT students.

A 2021 bill to bar transgender girls from girls' school sports teams passed the House 69 to 25 and the Senate 27 to 20 and was vetoed by Governor Doug Burgum on 21 April 2021. Two bills signed in April 2023 ban individuals assigned male at birth from female sports and athletics in schools and in higher education respectively.

Providing gender-affirming care to minors is illegal under a bill passed by a veto-proof majority on 5 April 2023.

A June 2021 committee regulation bans conversion therapy by social workers, psychologists and counselors.
tangentialFactors:
A 2022 Public Religion Research Institute poll found 78 percent of North Dakota residents supported an anti-discrimination law covering sexual orientation and gender identity and 22 percent opposed. In July 2020 North Dakota Republican delegates adopted a party platform opposing any civil rights protections for LGBTQ people and accusing transgender people of preying on women and LGBTQ people of recruiting children; many delegates condemned the platform, and Governor Doug Burgum opposed it as divisive, saying all North Dakotans deserve to be treated equally and live free of discrimination.

Perceptions of gender and sexuality within Native American tribes in the state differ from those of people of European descent, with traditions of third-gender people, also called two-spirit, who perform tasks and wear clothes considered gender non-conforming. These are identified as skuxát among the Arikara and miati and mihdeke among the Hidatsa and Mandan, and wįktą, winkta and wíŋkte among the Assiniboine, Dakota and Lakota.
localsOnly:
North Dakota's constitution and statutes previously restricted marriage to one man and one woman; proceedings in Ramsay v. Dalrymple were suspended in January 2015. The Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians legalized marriage for same-sex couples on its reservation by a 6 to 2 vote in August 2020.

Fargo has protected city employees on the basis of sexual orientation since 2001 and Jamestown does so as well; Grand Forks has protected city employees and applicants and rental housing since 2013. A Senate bill to ban sexual-orientation discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations passed 25 to 22 on 17 February 2015 but failed in the House.

Individuals may adopt, with no express ban on LGBTQ people or same-sex couples, though state law expressly allows private adoption agencies to discriminate on the basis of sincerely held religious belief; a 1980s Supreme Court ruling that made parental sexual orientation decisive in custody was reversed in 2003. Lesbian couples have access to in vitro fertilization, and state law recognises the non-genetic, non-gestational mother as a legal parent after donor insemination irrespective of marital status. Gestational surrogacy is expressly permitted for intended parents whether same-sex or different-sex; traditional surrogacy is prohibited.
outOfScopeNotes:
A March 2023 bill that would have allowed businesses to refuse service on any grounds based on a religious objective alone passed the legislature and awaited gubernatorial action; the source does not record the outcome, so the current status of that measure is unresolved.

The 2023 birth-certificate law's accompanying regulations were rejected, and the source does not establish which rule is applied to applications in practice: the 2023 surgical requirement or the 2008 sex-conversion-operation regulation.

The penalty provision in HB 1522 is recorded in the legislative overview without its terms. No enforcement action under North Dakota's bathroom-restriction law is documented in the sources reviewed.
